acceptance_criteria: Record upstream repository URL, latest stable release tag, commit SHA, release date, supported runtime/install paths, and source snapshot provenance in the compatibility matrix.

Inventory in-scope CLI, configuration, agent loop, provider routing, tools/MCP, persistence, Python integrations, API/streaming, memory/history, releases, and resource controls; each row names source locations and is either tested, pending, or explicitly excluded.
Run the upstream test/build checks appropriate to the clean pinned checkout and record exact commands/results; do not modify upstream.
Define at least two repeatable workload profiles and capture resource baseline metadata (hardware, OS, runtime, concurrency, dataset, duration, CPU, RSS, throughput, tail latency).
Update HRS-002 through HRS-004 with concrete source-grounded scope and dependencies; no claims of compatibility or speedup without evidence.

Identify the exact upstream Hermes test framework and suite revision; run it unchanged against the pinned Python reference, then route the same cases to Rust through a compatibility adapter. Publish per-case and aggregate score comparison with the same test IDs/denominator, explicit skip/exclusion reasons, raw outputs, and harness SHA. Rust-native tests are supplementary; supported-case score must be no lower than Python baseline.
description: Pin the current upstream Hermes Agent release, inspect its real repository surface and test/config/API contracts, and capture a reproducible resource baseline before implementation architecture is selected. See specs/HERMES_RS_COMPATIBILITY.md and specs/COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.md.
reasoning: Establish a pinned, evidence-backed compatibility and resource baseline before choosing architecture or claiming parity.
title: Baseline upstream Hermes scope and resource profile

acceptance_criteria: Inventory SQL, schema, transaction, locking, WAL, backup, and file-format assumptions from pinned Hermes source.
Specify a backend shim with standard SQLite as a maintained backend and PostgreSQL explicitly optional.

Benchmark the existing SQLite baseline against a viable SQLite-compatible Rust engine (Turso only if compatibility gates permit) on equal workloads and publish reproducible correctness/performance results.

If PostgreSQL is in supported scope, implement and test SQLite-to-PostgreSQL and PostgreSQL-to-SQLite import/export on representative data, including unsupported-type handling, integrity checks, backup, and rollback.
Do not switch the default backend or label an alternate as drop-in without parity, durability, migration, and rollback tests.
description: Design a persistence/backend boundary while preserving standard SQLite; compare candidate SQLite-compatible Rust engines (including Turso) and optional PostgreSQL on Hermes-shaped workloads. Define migration tools and round-trip guarantees.
reasoning: Preserve standard SQLite while testing whether a SQLite-compatible Rust engine helps; PostgreSQL is optional and requires round-trip migration tools.
title: Specify persistence shim and evaluate SQLite, Turso, and optional PostgreSQL

acceptance_criteria: Inventory Python library and extension points in pinned upstream source, including required Python version, packaging, native extensions, callbacks, and async behavior.
Document which integrations remain Python-native and which need bindings or process/protocol adapters, with explicit non-support cases.
Implement one end-to-end proof using an actually identified, in-scope Python library and test calls, data conversion, error propagation, and lifecycle.
Publish install/build commands and compatibility matrix entries; do not claim generic CPython ABI compatibility unless demonstrated.
description: Choose and prove a narrow interop mechanism for existing Python libraries against the Rust core. Separate Python packages/adapters from the Rust implementation and state the supported Python/ABI boundary.
reasoning: Existing Python libraries must remain usable through narrow, tested adapters without claiming unsupported CPython or ABI compatibility.
title: Define Python interoperability boundary and prove one library integration

acceptance_criteria: Create a repeatable pinned-tag/source-diff workflow covering release notes, source, public APIs, configuration, tests, and migrations.
Add fixture tests proving a known upstream change is surfaced and produces a traceable parity item or an explicit no-action rationale.
Define version mapping and supported-upstream range; publish known compatibility gaps on each release.
Add release gates for tests, compatibility status, database migration/rollback, provenance, and documented unsupported surfaces.
Demonstrate the workflow against a real upstream release tag and retain its report as a project artifact.
description: Track upstream Hermes releases and meaningful source changes, maintain parity tasks, and gate Hermes RS releases on explicit compatibility and rollback evidence.
reasoning: Track each upstream Hermes release and turn changed behavior into traceable parity work, compatibility evidence, and explicit gaps.
title: Build upstream release tracking and parity release gate
